newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba Pool would consider other joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba Pool would consider other joint venture.

text.p: One of Canada's largest grain handling firm would consider entering other joint ventures such as the one it announced with a rival firm on Wednesday, Manitoba Pool Elevators president Charlie Swanson said.
"Yes, if it makes good business sense, certainly both organizations I think would be prepared to consider it (other joint ventures)," Swanson told Reuters in a telephone interview.
MPE and Pioneer Grain Co Ltd earlier Wednesday announced the construction of a 12,000-tonne grain terminal and farm service centre near Roblin, on Manitoba's northwest grainbelt.
The facility will cost C$5-C$6 million to build, he said.
The high through put terminal could handle up to 140,000 tonnes of grain each year on 11 to 12 turnovers of inventory, Swanson said.
"That's certainly possible with a 50-(rail)car spot," he added.
Pioneer vice president Jim Weir was not immediately available for comment on other possible joint ventures.
